title: Early activation cohort credit sketches
content:
Purpose: quick sketches for a one-off early-activation credit program targeted at new signups (first 14 days). Goal is to cheaply increase first-week engagement and surface high-LTV flows. Not a final proposal — just back-of-envelope numbers to sanity check possible bands and triggers.

Assumptions / baseline inputs (rough):
- Average paid token price (hosted marginal cost estimate): $0.0006 per 1k tokens = $6e-7 per token (GPU + infra amortized for short sessions).
- Typical new-user session: 1,200 tokens (prompt + responses).
- Avg sessions per new user in week 1 (organic): 3.
- Conversion to paid after 30d (no credits): 1.6%. Target uplift to justify credit spend: +0.6–1.0 ppt.
- Target CAC on credits budget per converted user: $12–$20 (we prefer <$15 in early test).

Quick math (per-new-user cost if we credit entire first-week sessions):
- tokens/week = 1,200 * 3 = 3,600 tokens.
- cost/week = 3,600 * $6e-7 = $0.00216 (that's tiny; shows hosted marginal cost is tiny per token)
- That implies we could give a lot of nominal tokens for very low direct infra cost — but we need to include overhead (metrics, storage, rate-limit abuse, fraud). Suggest add 10x overhead multiplier for expected real-world operational/waste costs -> effective cost ~= $0.0216 per user-week.

That explains why earlier sketches that priced credits by token-value looked weirdly cheap. Key constraints are not marginal token cost; they are 1) perceived value to users, 2) amortized marketing/ops cost for credits, 3) downstream usage patterns (if credits drive heavy API usage or long KV-cached sessions).

Credit design options (sketches):
1) Starter Funnel Pack (time-limited): 5,000 credits valid 14 days.
   - Perceived value: headline "~5k tokens" (good for 3–4 full sessions).
   - Direct infra cost (w/10x ops overhead): 5,000 * $6e-7 * 10 = $0.003.
   - Marketing/alloc rounding -> estimate P&L cost = $0.20 per user (include attribution and fraud buffer).
   - Target: drive day-1 retention +20%, week-1 sessions +35%.

2) Session Boost (event-triggered): 2 free sessions (capped at 1,500 tokens each) unlocked after completing onboarding step.
   - Max tokens = 3,000 -> infra cost w/overhead = 3,000 * $6e-7 * 10 = $0.0018.
   - Perceived UX value higher (concrete "free sessions" messaging).
   - Operational risk: prone to gaming by scripts — needs device+ip heuristics.

3) Timed Long Tail Credits: 10,000 credits but usage throttled to 1 session per 6 hours. Valid 30 days.
   - More durable engagement; discourages burst abuse.
   - Effective infra cost still low; P&L reserve ~ $0.40 for overhead + activation subsidy.

Conversion modeling (super rough cohort sim):
- Baseline conversion = 1.6% (control).
- If Starter Funnel drives +0.7ppt -> conversion = 2.3% (relative +44%).
- If average LTV of a converted user = $320 (ARR-weighted), marginal revenue per new signup uplift = 0.007 * 320 = $2.24 incremental revenue.
- If we spend $0.20 per user on credits, ROI = 2.24 / 0.20 = 11.2x incremental revenue per dollar of credits (naive).
- Sensitivity: if uplift is only +0.2ppt -> revenue = 0.002 * 320 = $0.64; ROI = 3.2x. Still attractive.

Edge cases and flags:
- Fraud/abuse: small infra cost hides fraud risk. Plan to set fraud reserve (~10–20% of credits budget) and monitor: slack #growth flagged: suspicious signups on day 0.
- Cost shifting: Credits used on embeddings or heavy multimodal endpoints have different unit costs. Need per-product multipliers in allocation rules (e.g., embeddings *5 cost factor).
- Dedicated vs hosted customers: credits only make sense for hosted tier. For dedicated/private customers, need a different onboarding subsidy (discount coupon, pilot credits applied to invoices).

Operational mechanics (implementation sketch):
- Token-credit mapping: 1 credit = 1 token (keep mapping simple).
- Credit buckets: onboarding_5k, session_boost_2x, longtail_10k. Metadata includes expire_at, grant_reason, source_campaign.
- Grant triggers: sign-up, email-verified, complete-first-onboarding-step, referral-accept.
- Throttles and anti-abuse: max redemption per device_id, IP rate-limit, suspicious pattern flagging to SRE/Trust.
- Instrumentation: attach credit_id to request traces so console can break down retention by credit type.

Monitoring and experiments:
- Primary metrics: day-1 retention, week-1 sessions, 30d conversion to paid, churn at 90d for converted cohort.
- Secondary metrics: abuse rate (redemptions flagged), cost per converted user, revenue uplift per cohort.
- Experiment plan: A/B test Starter Funnel vs Control vs Session Boost. N per arm ~ 25k new signups to detect +0.5ppt uplift with 80% power (back-of-envelope; run power calc properly).

Quick TODOs: 
- [ ] Wire up a small prototype: grant starter_5k on signup in staging, add trace id to console. (Assign: Samira)
- [ ] Draft fraud/reserve policy and set quota enforcement knobs (Assign: Liam)
- [ ] Build simple dashboard (metric: cost-per-converted-user) and a tag filter for credit_id. (Assign: Asha)

Notes & open questions: 
- Should credits be convertible to trial days for developer accounts? Could broaden appeal to API-first users who care about time not tokens.
- Psychological framing matters: "5k free tokens" vs "2 free sessions" may convert differently — need copy experiment.
- How to treat returned/unused credits for accounting? Need finance input on breakage recognition window.

References: 
- PRIC-421: earlier cohort test notes (linked above).
- Slack thread: #growth-activation (June-Nov 2024) — lots of anecdotal feedback about session-style incentives.

Bottom line: infrastructure cost per user for modest credit packs is tiny; the real levers are perceived product value and anti-abuse. If we can keep operational overhead and fraud low, even small uplifts in conversion justify moderately generous credit packages. This doc is just a scratchpad — next step is a lightweight A/B test spec and an operational playbook for throttling and monitoring.

Rough signature: Asha P. (notes — will iterate)
